title: Regulatory prior-art extract record
description: ONE instrument, deep-read into its obligations. Frontmatter plus body in one file, and the frontmatter stays FLAT: nested machine structure means the record wants to be JSON. Throughout this artifact `requirement` means a LEGAL OBLIGATION, never a product requirement.

instrument_id.description: Resolver-scoped and filename-safe by construction. A candidate is NEVER given an id it did not read: where an instrument has no registry identifier, `WEB-` is the honest fallback, and inventing a registry number is the single worst thing this survey can do.

as_of.description: The date the TEXT was true -- the consolidation date. NOT when it was fetched: collapsing the two makes a five-year-stale consolidation look current.

retrieved_at.description: When this record fetched it. A different fact from `as_of`, deliberately.

skipped.description: Present iff `outcome: skipped`. A bail STILL WRITES the record.

authority.description: Four tiers, strongest first. Ranking and dedupe input ONLY -- never a cut.

eli.description: A resolvable URI, stored as a FIELD and never used as a filename -- it contains slashes.

cfr_citation.description: Contains spaces and dots, so it is not filename-safe as written.

standard_number.description: For a paywalled standard the NUMBER is a citable identifier even though the TEXT is not retrievable.

applies_from_date.description: SEPARATE from `in_force_date`, because staged application is common and load-bearing: an instrument binding in fourteen months is an architecture constraint NOW and a compliance obligation LATER.

text_retrievable.description: `paywalled` is a LEGITIMATE terminal state: a record may name the instrument, set this, and carry no quoted requirement at all. Saying `this applies and its text costs money to read` is a genuine finding. NEVER paraphrase a paywalled clause.

applies_because.description: The scope condition that makes it bind THIS product -- not a category. `healthcare products must comply` is true of a category and establishes nothing about this one.

requirements.description: The legal obligations read out of the instrument. Empty is legitimate where the text was not retrievable.

id.description: `<instrument_id>#r<N>`, minted at extract time after the read. The prefix is how synthesis groups by instrument, so an id that does not extend its own instrument's orphans the requirement.

obligation_ref.description: The article, section or clause this obligation sits at.

requirement.description: What the instrument obliges, in this survey's sense of the word: a LEGAL obligation, never a product requirement.

verbatim_anchor.description: A SHORT quoted phrase, never the whole provision -- the whole provision is a licence problem and is not extraction. Null on a paywalled instrument.

trigger_condition.description: What starts the clock, for anything with a duration.

dimension.description: A CLOSED enum, each member declaring its unit, its order and its comparator. `consent_basis` and `residency_constraint` are NOT ordered: two requirements disagreeing there are a CONFLICT and never a merge. Null where the obligation is not on a comparable axis at all.

stated_standard.description: NULLABLE on purpose. `appropriate`, `reasonable` and `state of the art` are not specifications and must not be reproduced as though they were -- a null here is a fact the conflict lens reads.

duration_value.description: ISO-8601 (`P7D`, `P6Y`). Storing the duration in one form removes the unit-parsing step entirely, which is what lets hours be compared against years.

control_ids.description: Externally-owned control ids, OSCAL lowercase-dotted (`at-2.2`) and never prose casing (`AT-2(2)`). Both spellings are real and refer to the same control, so mixing them silently splits a merge group in two.

requires_counsel.description: `ambiguous` implies this, and the gate checks it mechanically.
